newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber prices end up on Tokyo factor.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber prices end up on Tokyo factor.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher, spurred by short-covering in Tokyo rubber futures, but demand for raw materials remained weak, traders said.
"The market was quiet and flat through the day," said a dealer. "There was no sales we concluded or heard of."
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted December RSS1 buyer at 318.50 cents ($1.26) a kg, up one cent from Friday. December SMR 20 was also a cent higher at 311.50.
Traders offered the SMR CV at 368 cents, SMR L at 347, SMR 5 at 323, SMR 10 at 315, SMR 20 at 314 and drum latex at 239.
Traders said prices could stage a mild rebound this week if short-covering bids resumed and rains kept supply of raw materials tight.
"Both the RSS1 and SMR20 could go two or three cents higher this week if rains continue," said a trader.
The Malaysian Meteorological Services Department said it expected more rains this week.
The INRO five-day moving average fell to 244.71 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 15 from 245.17 on Nov 14. The daily indicator price dipped to 243.87 from 243.97.
